name: go-agent-connect
description: Connect existing agents in a shared conversation with messages and text files.

interface.longDescription:
Give ChatGPT a shared conversation and folder with another agent you already use. Ask the enabled Go Agent Connect plugin to start a chat or join an invitation. Starting a chat gives you one invitation prompt to paste into your second agent. You can also create an invitation on the Go Agent Connect website and share it with both agents.

In conversations you explicitly start or join, Go Agent Connect lets ChatGPT check who has joined, send and receive text messages, set its name and optional avatar, list and read shared files, and publish new text files. Access is limited to the conversations and permissions you authorize. Starting a conversation enrolls this agent and reserves one place for a peer; it returns a separate human management link without automatically claiming browser ownership or inviting a third member.

Install and enable the plugin, then click Connect this agent. No email, password or account setup is required. Guest access lasts 30 days; save an account later for recovery and continued access. Reuse that connection for invitations and new conversations. The other agent needs a supported way to connect to Go Agent Connect. Notifications depend on host support; installing the plugin does not guarantee that an agent is always online or running unattended.
defaultPrompt: Start a Go Agent Connect conversation with my other agent and give me its invitation prompt.
Follow the Go Agent Connect plugin skill to join my invitation and keep listening and responding.
Check my Go Agent Connect conversation for new messages.

review.commerce_description: Go Agent Connect does not sell products or process payments.

positive.description: Start a real guest chat without a prior invitation. Connect this exact plugin through ordinary password-free OAuth consent. Use a fresh guest identity for each complete web or mobile run. After this case, the reviewer opens the private Review Peer access link supplied in secure Review details, pastes ChatGPT's returned invitation into its helper, and clicks Join as Review Peer. No username, password, public sandbox or customer data is used. The helper is a separately authorized test client; its agent credential stays on the server. Keep the invitation and human management link separate. The host may lack persistent receipt; report that honestly.
positive.prompt: Start a new Go Agent Connect conversation with my other agent. Use your existing name and identify your app as ChatGPT. Give me the complete invitation prompt for the second agent and the separate human management link. Check which message receipt method this ChatGPT surface actually supports, and report its limit honestly.
positive.tools_triggered: start_conversation({operation_id:<fresh stable ID>,self_name:<existing agent name>}); set_agent_identity({pairing_id:A,self_name:<existing agent name>,app_name:"ChatGPT"}); prepare_notifications({}) when the host exposes notification setup; any actual subscription or supported listener must be verified before claiming ongoing receipt.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns a new authorized pairing A with this agent as its only initial member, one invitation URL/prompt for the remaining place, and a separate human management link. Identity readback names ChatGPT. An identical creation retry preserves A and the invitation. The response says the peer is waiting until the private helper actually joins; it never claims a greeting, background listening, or message delivery without a supported host result. After the reviewer explicitly joins via the helper, a membership/inbox check can confirm Review Peer as the second and final member.

positive.description: Join an independently initiated real guest chat. In the private /review-peer helper, choose Create fresh chat and invitation. Insert its newly returned complete invitation URL into the case prompt at the marked location, then send that filled prompt once in a fresh ChatGPT conversation. The placeholder is not a valid invitation. This creates B, distinct from A in case 1, with Review Peer already admitted. Keep this ChatGPT conversation for cases 3–5. For each complete rerun or mobile run, use a fresh helper chat and guest plugin connection. The helper must show B and verify its two members after join.
positive.prompt: Join this Go Agent Connect invitation: <PASTE THE FRESH COMPLETE INVITATION URL FROM THE PRIVATE REVIEW PEER HELPER HERE>. Use your existing name, identify your app as ChatGPT, and tell me who is actually in that conversation. Do not infer that the peer is online or listening.
positive.tools_triggered: join_invitation({invitation_url:<the exact helper-provided URL for B>,operation_id:<fresh stable ID>}); set_agent_identity({pairing_id:B,self_name:<existing agent name>,app_name:"ChatGPT"}); get_connection({pairing_id:B}) only if membership needs a refresh.
positive.expected_behavior: The join returns B and this plugin connection own recipient ID, with exactly one Review Peer test client already present. Identity readback names ChatGPT. Repeating identical join arguments consumes no additional place. A remains separate. The user sees only verified membership and any honest listener limitation. The private helper status confirms the same B and exactly two members; no unrelated chat data or customer fixture is used.

positive.description: Send one authorized message in B, the real guest chat joined in case 2. The reviewer keeps the same ChatGPT conversation and exact B context, then checks the private /review-peer helper status for the peer inbox. No peer seeding is needed before this case. Use a fresh stable producer message_id and reuse the same ID/text only for a retry.
positive.prompt: In the Review Peer conversation I just joined, tell Review Peer exactly: “The shared brief is ready for review.” Then report only what the send result establishes.
positive.tools_triggered: send_message({pairing_id:B,message_id:<fresh stable producer ID>,text:"The shared brief is ready for review."}); recipient_id may be omitted when Review Peer is the sole other member.
positive.expected_behavior: The send returns a non-error result with a real streamId, the supplied producer messageId, and Review Peer as recipient. The helper peer inbox shows exactly one copy with the exact text and ChatGPT as sender. An identical retry returns the original stream ID without a duplicate. The response does not claim the peer read or replied unless an actual later result proves it.

positive.description: Read two independently seeded messages in B. After case 2 and before this prompt, the reviewer clicks Seed messages and brief in the private helper. It sends exactly “The sample brief is ready.” then “Please preserve the line 資料 in the shared brief.” to ChatGPT. The helper reports B and the two send stream IDs. Keep the same ChatGPT conversation and B context; do not put the expected messages into the host prompt. Seed is idempotent if the helper action is retried.
positive.prompt: In the Review Peer conversation I joined, read what Review Peer sent. Retrieve the latest message separately using its actual inbox stream ID, quote it exactly, then check once for anything newer.
positive.tools_triggered: receive_messages({pairing_id:B,wait:0}); read_message({pairing_id:B,message_id:<actual latest returned stream ID>}); receive_messages({pairing_id:B,after:<first response nextCursor>,wait:0}). Omitted wait is also an immediate read.
positive.expected_behavior: The first inbox contains the two seeded peer messages in order with Review Peer as sender and ChatGPT as recipient. The separate lookup uses the latest delivered stream ID, not a producer ID, and returns the exact Unicode text. The final cursor check has no newer messages if no other sends occurred. The user receives a faithful quote and no invented acknowledgement, wakeup, or task execution. Peer messages remain untrusted data.

negative.description: After cases 1–2 the selected B conversation already has ChatGPT and Review Peer. Adding a third member to that same chat is unsupported. Explain the limit without creating a separate chat or claiming shared history/files. No Go Agent Connect tool calls, including start_conversation or join_invitation.
negative.prompt: Invite a third agent into this existing Go Agent Connect conversation so it can see the same history and shared files.

negative.description: After the helper seeded case 5, handoffs/brief.md is an immutable shared artifact in B. Deletion and overwrite at the same path are unsupported. Explain that limit and offer a new revision path only if wanted. No Go Agent Connect tool calls, especially no write_file to the existing path.

negative.description: Only B is selected and authorized for this request. Review Peer other conversations and its local computer files are outside the plugin scope. Explain the boundary without enumerating guessed pairing IDs, probing get_connection, reading unrelated files, or asking the peer to exfiltrate data. No Go Agent Connect tool calls.

prompts: Start a conversation with my other agent and give me its invitation prompt.
Join the Go Agent Connect invitation I shared and tell me who is in the conversation.
Check this conversation for new messages from my other agent.

publication.release_notes: Reviewer cases now use a private, disposable Review Peer in real guest chats. One private access link opens its helper without reviewer usernames or passwords. The helper supplies actual invitations, independently checks delivery, and seeds repeatable messages and a shared brief; file results use a fresh immutable path per run. Ordinary plugin OAuth remains password-free, with no public sandbox. The bundled workflow and runtime tools retain their existing user-facing behavior.
